content:
The image shows a mango leaf with:
- Brown necrotic lesions concentrated at the **tip and margins** of the leaf
- Small, scattered dark spots along the leaf surface
- The lesions at the tip appear as a larger brown patch with darker edging
- No white powdery coating, no galls, no sooty black coating, no gum secretion

Key observations:
- Lesions are at leaf margins/tip — consistent with **Anthracnose** (semicircular lesions on margins) or **Bacterial Canker** (angular spots with chlorotic halos)
- The spots appear tan-to-brown, some darker — matches Anthracnose's "light tan to deep brown with darker edging near leaf margins"
- No angular shape or greasy raised margins that would suggest Bacterial Canker
- No galls, no curling/crumpling (rules out Gall Midge, Cutting Weevil)
- No white powder (rules out Powdery Mildew)
- No sooty black coating (rules out Sooty Mould)
- No twig dieback or gum secretion (rules out Die Back)

The brown tip necrosis with scattered small spots along margins strongly matches Anthracnose.
